anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : contention for hot buffer-cache pages, latches, pins, and dirty-page slots stalls CPU threads and throttles page access.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : physical or logical corruption inside data or index pages makes on-disk structures unreliable and can force scan fall-backs or error aborts.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : shortages or instability in sockets, listener threads, or network bandwidth delay or terminate client/server communication.

When all three conditions coexist, the system presents a layered, self-reinforcing failure pattern. Clients observe sporadic connection timeouts, authentication delays, and mid-stream result stalls. Sessions that do connect frequently hang on buffer-busy or page-latch waits; when pages are finally read, checksum mismatches or broken index links trigger retries, error propagation, or crash-recovery cycles. These extra retries enlarge connection pools and keep server backends alive longer, further depleting socket and worker resources. Corruption-induced plan shifts from targeted index probes to full scans explode buffer-pool churn, pinning and dirtying more pages and sharply increasing latch spin as many sessions converge on the few remaining uncorrupted root or allocation pages. Meanwhile, network congestion prolongs result transmission, extending buffer-pin lifetimes and exacerbating contention hot spots.

Causally, page and index corruption can force workload patterns (full scans, repeated fetch attempts) that inflate buffer-cache pressure; the resulting latch contention lengthens query execution times, which in turn holds network connections open and propagates retry storms that exhaust listener backlogs and socket tables. Simultaneously, network slowdowns raise session counts and idle-in-transaction periods, compounding buffer residency and latch hold times. The vicious cycle among corrupted storage structures, in-memory contention, and connection saturation rapidly degrades throughput and makes isolation of any single fault difficult, driving the database into a multi-layered degradation spiral.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the number of TCP keepalive messages that can be lost before the server connection to the client is considered dead.
entry.trigger_condition: The number of lost TCP keepalive probes reaches tcp_keepalives_count on systems supporting TCP_KEEPCNT.
entry.workload_impact: The server can consider the client connection dead after the configured keepalive failure threshold.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
